evidence.note: Built an independent reference oracle (ref.py) right after a first kernel, then ran a correctness harness against it — reference-before-optimization staging with a concrete match check.

Verified the kernel component-by-component (layernorm, contraction reshape, gating) and fixed/re-ran correctness before touching performance — a straightforward-correct milestone with per-component done-checks.
Only after correctness passed did it write bench.py and begin benchmarking contraction strategies — a clear transition from a correctness milestone into a separate latency/optimization track.

During the long optimization phase, risky numeric changes (bf16 projections, bf16 output) were each gated by explicit accuracy re-checks, and a full correctness+latency sweep was rerun — recurring exit tests that localize fast-but-wrong regressions.
Optimization stage itself decomposed into per-shape/per-kernel tuning (front/back/contract config sweeps, N=2048 profiling) rather than one monolithic fast push.

reasoning: The trajectory shows explicit ordered stages well beyond the level-5 anchor: an independent reference oracle, a component-verified straightforward kernel matched to it, and only then a lengthy optimization track — each with rough-to-concrete success checks (correctness harness, sweeps, per-change accuracy gates). It approaches level 8 because risky optimizations (bf16) were consistently gated by correctness re-checks that localize regressions, and the optimization phase was decomposed into per-shape tuning; it falls short of 8/10 because I cannot confirm a distinct 'naive kernel matches reference across the full grid' milestone was frozen before optimization began, and there's no evidence of explicit risk-sequencing (hardest Cauchy/large-N cases first). This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.
